races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Capitano Josepi
runners_data.note: Unexposed 2yo trained by Kevin & Lauren Frost — unknown running style and going preference means significant uncertainty, but fresh and capable of improvement on debut-type evidence; anything from this stable capable of a price upset.

runners_data.name: Del Pearo
runners_data.note: Ran sixth at Goodwood last time, John Ryan yard showing 2/6 T14 form; natural hold-up runner who, in this traffic-heavy field, is unlikely to find the back of the field available and will be racing in a position that is not his own — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Extragalactic
runners_data.note: William Haggas is in career-best T14 form (8/46) and this unraced or lightly-raced 2yo carries notebook status; running style unknown but pedigree from a top stable on soft ground makes it an obvious contender if it handles conditions.

runners_data.name: Pressured
runners_data.note: Finished ninth at Goodwood last time, a confirmed hold-up horse who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; soft ground is unlikely to remedy that stamina concern and the pace shape here does not play to its strengths.

runners_data.name: Strong Performance
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who faded when eighth at Goodwood on good ground; William Knight has reasonable T14 figures but this horse's finishing pattern is a red flag on soft going over 7f — the conditions will expose any stamina limitation more harshly.

runners_data.name: Top Cote
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with a handicap mark of 70 and previous form figures of 2-3-4 over shorter trips at Goodwood; racing from a prominent style on soft going suits the race shape it creates, though the step up from 5-6f and 104 days off are the key questions.

runners_data.name: Hidden Beyond
runners_data.note: Third on debut at Sandown over 7f, Charles Hills stable (2/21 T14), Daniel Muscutt booked — soft going on debut evidence is unknown but the course and distance profile matches and Hidden Beyond sits firmly in the prominent/front-tracking beneficiary bracket for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Perfect Love
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's runner finished eighth at Sandown last time and is a confirmed hold-up horse with a fade pattern — 40 days off and soft conditions over 7f look a tough ask given what the form already shows about its finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Mystic Unicorn
runners_data.note: Recent form of 9-5 at Sandown (both on soft/standard), and a genuine hold-up runner; this field cannot push all rear-end types to the back, so Mystic Unicorn is likely to race closer to the pace than it wants — that positional compromise undermines its chance materially.

runners_data.name: Rocsane
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (5-3-2-2 in form), with a sim-going marker showing 1 win from 4 on soft-equivalent ground and 0 wins 0 places on the nose; Silvestre De Sousa is the asset here, but Rocsane's natural hold-up style will be compromised by midfield positioning in this crowded race shape.

runners_data.name: Theft
runners_data.note: George Scott's 2yo ran fifth at Sandown (7f, standard) and seventh at Goodwood — unknown going response on soft, but Scott's T14 of 2/24 is modest; running style unconfirmed, form is modest, and needs significant improvement to figure.

races.paceDynamic: Top Cote is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride out uncontested from the gates and set a sustainable, controlled tempo over Yarmouth's flat 7f on soft ground. That soft surface will blunt any natural acceleration from closers and reward horses who travel comfortably in the first half of the race rather than those asked to make up ground late against the dead ground. With Top Cote dictating an honest but unhurried gallop, the race favours prominent or near-prominent types who can slot in just behind the leader, avoid the soft-ground attrition of chasing from deep, and produce a sustained finish rather than a short, sharp kick. Three runners — Mystic Unicorn, Del Pearo, and Rocsane — are true hold-up horses redistributed to the midfield on the map because this race cannot accommodate all rear-end types at the back; they are unlikely to secure their natural positions and their chances in a shape that rewards pace-reliance must be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Top Cote Leads, Stays Fresh
scenarios.trigger: If Top Cote bowls along uncontested and the soft ground keeps the tempo honest enough that prominent trackers cannot exploit a pace collapse.
scenarios.body: Top Cote controls the fractions from stall, the soft going ensures no one burns him off from behind, and horses who travel prominently in the slipstream — particularly unexposed types from strong stables — get the run of the race and hit the rising ground with petrol still in the tank.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground produces a war of attrition from halfway and the prominent horses use their early position to post relentless sectionals that finish off hold-up rivals.
scenarios.body: Top Cote and his immediate shadows grind out a true test of stamina in the conditions, and horses who have shown form on or near soft going and are close enough to the pace emerge as the beneficiaries when the field strings out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly-raced runners (Extragalactic, Capitano Josepi, Theft) produces a step forward in form that their bare figures have not yet advertised.
scenarios.body: With William Haggas or George Scott horses carrying notebook status and the race shape offering a clean target to aim at, an unexposed runner who has been tutored for exactly this scenario can pick off a tiring field with a single, decisive move.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mop Up
scenarios.trigger: If Top Cote and the prominent pack collectively overcook the early fractions on soft ground, leaving a rare opening for genuine rear-runners to pick up late.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally unlikely given Top Cote's confirmed tendency to set a measured pace and the fact that the true hold-up horses (Del Pearo, Mystic Unicorn, Rocsane) have been redistributed forward and may not even secure deep positions; Rocsane's soft-going course form gives her the best residual claim if it does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Top Cote has been off 104 days and steps up sharply in trip from 5-6f to 7f on soft ground — watch for Jonny Peate being forced to inject early pace or alternatively being caught flat-footed if freshness turns to greenness, as this would entirely alter the race shape.

Extragalactic (Haggas, 8/46 T14) is unknown quantity but the trainer's current strike rate demands respect — watch for this runner drifting or firming sharply in the market pre-race as the clearest real-time signal on its true readiness.

Del Pearo, Mystic Unicorn, and Rocsane are all genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield by the race shape — watch for a congested middle section in the back straight as these runners attempt to find their feet in unfamiliar positions, creating potential traffic risks for everything around them.

Hidden Beyond's debut third came at Sandown, a very different track profile to Yarmouth's flat, straight 7f — watch whether Daniel Muscutt elects to track Top Cote prominently from the outset, as that tactical call will determine whether it gets the pace scenario it needs.

Soft ground at Yarmouth is confirmed across all races today — watch the winning times relative to standard to gauge whether conditions are genuinely testing or merely soft in name, as a faster-than-expected surface would open the door slightly for hold-up runners currently discounted.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Exceeding Expectations In Construction Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Adrestia
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who should dictate throughout; Simon & Ed Crisford have her fresh off a 33-day break with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and her five-furlong course speed record is solid, though recent form figures of 6-7800 on faster ground must temper expectations on the soft.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Adrestia nonetheless rates highly on a speed figure of 95 and our rating of 98 puts her narrowly ahead at the head of this nine-runner field; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 33 days between runs leaves her fresh enough to go close from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's six-year-old returned to winning at five furlongs at Goodwood 14 days ago and arrives in excellent heart; his sim-going record shows one win from one soft run so the conditions need monitoring, but his prominent style means he will be perfectly positioned if Adrestia stops.
runners_data.comment: Rocking End's win three starts back reads well at this level, and he arrives fit on a 14-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 92 suggesting he retains ability; the risk is that consecutive fifth-place finishes since that win hint at a return to modest form.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's three-year-old won at Goodwood in June and has one soft-going start in her recent history; she sits right behind the leader naturally and a fresh mind from 31 days off could see her produce a sharp, clean finish if the fractions are honest.
runners_data.comment: Dazzling Haze won three starts back but has been unplaced in both runs since, and while she has experience over today's trip and going, the weight of 135 lb from stall two is a further test of whether she can rediscover that winning form.

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator by style whose sim-going record shows four runs in similar conditions with one placing, suggesting soft is not a problem; the 33-day break is manageable but he is relying on front runners tying up in a straight five-furlong track where that rarely happens cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Seven Questions won four starts back and has live claims stepping out from stall one carrying 134 lb, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour; the risk is that his last two outings both ended in unplaced efforts, so he needs to recapture that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: The headgear note (hg:p) and a win on good ground at Goodwood earlier in the season confirm ability at the trip; his soft-going record is thin from 15 comparable runs and he needs something to go wrong up front, which is against the grain of this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Michaela's Boy won three starts back but has since finished fourth and eighth, so consistency is the obvious concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 134 lb from stall six, and his official mark of 86 suggests he holds his own at this level if returning to that winning form.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old has three placed efforts on soft or good-to-soft going in her last five, making her the most proven of the prominent group in these conditions; Harry Davies rides and she maps genuinely close to the pace, which is exactly the profile this race rewards.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Kinswoman nonetheless brings solid credentials — she has run over today's trip and going before, returns fit on a 15-day turnaround, and our rating of 94 marks her out as a leading danger; the concern is that recent form has been patchy, with a fourth last time out and little improvement since a second five starts back.

runners_data.name: Hypnotised
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's three-year-old has placed twice at this trip on fast ground but has never encountered soft in five career starts, leaving a significant unknown; 15 days since last run is fine but the going is an untested variable for a horse who needs to finish fast.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures, Hypnotised faces a stiff task at 129 lb from stall seven, though back-to-back runner-up finishes show he retains some form, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: In reality a front-running type with a win at five furlongs on standard AW going, she finds herself squeezed into midfield on the map because the prominent slots are already filled; Ashley Lewis takes the 3lb claim but the horse will need luck in running from a position that does not suit her natural game.
runners_data.comment: Elara May has won once in her last five starts, with a fourth last time out and an eighth two starts back doing little to inspire confidence, and ranked seventh of nine on our figures she faces a stiff ask here, though she does at least bring distance and going experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Master
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's eight-year-old, a genuine hold-up horse in practice, has five runs in soft-ground conditions producing no wins and no places, which is a significant red flag; placed into the midfield map position rather than the rear, he carries a style-fit discount and the soft-going record makes him hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Fantasy Master heads into this off the back of a promising second last time out, though he ranks last on our figures in a field of nine and is hard to fancy at the weights; a winner four starts back, he has experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Adrestia is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should secure a comfortable, self-controlled gallop from the gates on soft ground over five furlongs at Yarmouth. Rocking Ends, Dazzling Haze, and Kinswoman are all naturally prominent types who will press for early position just behind, creating a compact front group rather than a genuinely contested pace. Soft ground will slow the tempo fractionally but Adrestia's uncontested lead means the pace is likely to be honest rather than frenetic, with the race developing into a test of both stamina and the ability to quicken from a covered position. This field holds more prominent types than can realistically all get their position — Elara May and Fantasy Master are true prominent and hold-up types respectively but are mapped to midfield given the traffic ahead of them, meaning Rocking Ends and Dazzling Haze are most likely to actually secure the positions immediately behind Adrestia. The race shape strongly favours horses that can sit close to a sustainable pace and produce a clean, relatively short finish — prominent racers who travel well in the box seat are the prime profile to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Adrestia controls, holds
scenarios.trigger: If Adrestia leads uncontested and the soft ground blunts the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Adrestia dictates every fraction from the front with no pressure applied, and on soft ground a well-rated horse carrying tp headgear who travels within herself can simply stay on too strongly for rivals who need a target to aim at. Prominent types Rocking Ends and Dazzling Haze who track the leader are next best placed as they never lose contact and avoid ground-churning traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent sit-and-pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Adrestia's fractions are just quick enough on soft going to leave her vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting a length or two off the leader in a perfect stalking position gets first run when the pace softens, with Rocking Ends or Dazzling Haze benefiting most from that covered position. Kinswoman's soft-going form (three placed efforts at the trip in similar conditions) also makes her a serious threat in this shape as she arrives late from just off the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers swoop late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than expected and the front group tie up in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Soft ground and a packed prominent division could cause enough mid-race scrimmaging to create a brief cavalry charge, giving Hypnotised, Seven Questions, or Michaela's Boy a slim chance of getting home late. These are genuine hold-up or midfield operators, but they face the significant disadvantage of having to pick their way through a compacted bunch on a straight five-furlong track where gaps are hard to find.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution disrupts field
scenarios.trigger: If Elara May or Fantasy Master fight for positions ahead of where they are mapped and cause early crowding.
scenarios.body: Either horse burning energy to recover natural prominent ground would unsettle the mid-pack order and artificially compress the field, creating bumping and checks that could benefit a horse wide and clear on the outside. This is the lowest-probability shape because both horses are tagged as being pushed out of role and are unlikely to produce their best form from compromised positions.

watchPoints.text: Adrestia's recent form reads 6-7800 on good ground — watch whether she translates that speed to soft, because if she deflates inside the final furlong having led throughout, the entire race shape collapses for front-position traders.

Rocking Ends and Dazzling Haze are both genuine prominent types and will compete for the same ground immediately behind Adrestia in the first furlong — watch for any bumping or checking between stalls two through four that could compromise either runner early.

Elara May's jockey Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) may attempt to push forward from the gate to recover natural prominent ground; watch whether she burns excess energy in the first two furlongs fighting for a position the map cannot give her in this field.

Soft going at Yarmouth on a straight five furlongs tends to reward those who handle the conditions cleanly rather than those with raw early pace — watch for any horse that travels fluently in the first two furlongs, as they are likely to be the winner.

Three Robert Cowell runners (Seven Questions, Michaela's Boy, Fantasy Master, Dazzling Haze) share trainer and stable intelligence — watch the market for any significant move on the Cowell quartet as a signal of which runner the yard considers live.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Constructing Champions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rose Cotton
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with strong course and trip profile, two recent placed efforts at 1m2f on Standard/Soft, and Tom Clover's yard in 4-from-18 form over 14 days; unchallenged pace here is a significant tactical asset and soft ground is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Rose Cotton shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out and second three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her strong claims from stall five. The chief concern is that 47 days off the track may leave her just short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, held up naturally, and has placed at 1m2f on soft ground (form 3/12f/SOF) though winless in similar going; Jack Callan takes over for Dylan Cunha's yard which is firing at 6/26 over 14 days, but the hold-up style leaves him reliant on others making mistakes.
runners_data.comment: Patrol shaped with plenty of credit last time, finishing third nine days ago, and also ran second twice in recent starts — a consistent profile that makes him the one to beat here, even if he remains winless in his last six. Has run over today's trip and going, and carries 135 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Triple Double A
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's horse wears a tongue-tie and prefers to race prominently, though recent form on good ground at shorter trips (8f) raises questions about this 1m2f soft test; zero wins or places in similar going from 15 attempts is a concern and Luke Catton's 3lb claim partially compensates.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Triple Double A nonetheless carries a speed rating of 88 that marks him as one of the sharper threats in this field, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is a recent sequence of mid-to-rear finishes that is hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won at 1m2f on Standard ground (1/12f/STA) and has finished placed on soft in two attempts; Ashley Lewis's 3lb claim is useful, Marcus Tregoning's yard has only one runner in the past 14 days suggesting a deliberate preparation, and the trip and style suit this scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form with a win five starts back, but has finished third at best in her last four outings since; Twilight Moon has run over today's trip and going, carries 134 lb from stall seven, and represents a midfield profile that could see her involved without necessarily threatening the principals.

runners_data.name: Moonjid
runners_data.note: Has won at 1m (10f) on good ground and wears a hood, suggesting some headgear dependency, but this 1m2f trip is a step up in distance and soft going is new territory with limited evidence (3/15 in similar going, zero wins); Michael Appleby's yard in modest form at 1/15 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Moonjid has run over today's trip and going, and his win four starts back shows he can produce when conditions align, but three subsequent finishes of fourth, fifth and seventh in his last six starts suggest consistency remains elusive carrying 134 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has won twice on soft ground, most recently at 1m on soft, making him the most proven soft-ground performer in the field; 88 days off is a significant concern for Peter Chapple-Hyam's yard (0 runners in 14 days), but the soft-ground profile genuinely stands out.
runners_data.comment: Something Splendid landed a win five starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 79 lending him strong claims here; the main concern is that he has not raced in 88 days.

runners_data.name: Solanna
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt partners this seven-year-old for John Butler, who is 1/16 in 14-day form; Solanna won recently at Goodwood (1/10f/GOO) and has placed at 1m2f — a prominent racing style suits the likely shape and age brings no penalty here given current form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Solanna faces a stiff ask here, and that sixth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Arundel
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's horse returns after 351 days off, an enormous layoff that is the most significant flag in this field; hold-up by nature but placed in the map to midfield given the surplus of rear-runners — its true deep-closing style makes a first-time-out run after nearly a year highly speculative, even if soft form (2/10f/SOF) is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for nearly a year, Arundel faces a stiff task ranked eighth of nine on our figures, though he has run over today's distance and going before and that experience offers at least some slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's five-year-old wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping, meaning it is racing out of its natural zone; the horse's recent runs have been at shorter 8f trips on fast ground with only one similar-going run from 13 attempts, and Silvestre De Sousa cannot fully compensate for the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Man Of Desert faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a sound enough 18-day break carrying 126 lb from stall eight.

races.paceDynamic: Rose Cotton is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front over this 1m2f on soft ground at Yarmouth. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Man Of Desert and Arundel are true hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because Patrol, Moonjid and Something Splendid all want to come from behind and cannot all occupy the rear. With Rose Cotton unchallenged up front and soft ground likely to stretch the field early, the race will likely develop as a steady-to-moderate pace affair that turns into a stamina test from the home bend, with the genuine closers potentially hitting a congestion problem if they cannot find room. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Rose Cotton and pounce without needing a clear passage late — horses like Twilight Moon, Solanna and Triple Double A, who can sit close to the pace and benefit from a lack of genuine pressure on the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rose Cotton Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Cotton is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured pace on soft ground and kicks again turning for home.
scenarios.body: Rose Cotton's history of front-running at this course and trip, combined with a passive field behind her, creates a scenario where she steals the race with a sustained gallop no one can match; soft ground extends her stamina advantage and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Moon and/or Solanna track Rose Cotton closely and overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: These two prominent types have the form to sit a length or two off the pace and benefit from a soft-ground staying test once Rose Cotton begins to tire; Solanna's recent Goodwood win and Twilight Moon's course-trip form give both a strong profile in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the field bunches, enabling hold-up horses to produce a finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Moonjid and Something Splendid, who have soft-ground form and proven ability to finish from off the pace, would benefit if the tempo is so slow that even closers can mount a meaningful challenge from midfield; Something Splendid's two wins on soft ground give it a viable profile here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse, Redistributed Types Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Cotton sets a stronger pace than anticipated and the true hold-up horses (Man Of Desert, Arundel) find more room than mapped.
scenarios.body: Both Man Of Desert and Arundel are racing out of their natural role in this map, and the probability of this shape delivering is suppressed because they are not genuine prominent types; only a very specific pace collapse with a clear run would bring them into contention.

watchPoints.text: Rose Cotton (Jack Mitchell) is the only confirmed front-runner — if she gets a completely free lead she could steal this on soft ground and any drift wide from rivals early should be treated as a significant market signal.

Something Splendid (Marco Ghiani) returns after 88 days off and has the best soft-ground credentials in the race — watch the market closely pre-race, as any money for a horse trained by Chapple-Hyam after this break on favourable ground would be significant.

Arundel (Edward Greatrex) has not run for 351 days — Ed Dunlop horses returning after extended absences should be monitored for market support, and any move in the market would suggest the yard has this one ready despite the layoff.

Twilight Moon (Ashley Lewis, 3lb claim) and Solanna (Daniel Muscutt) are both prominent types who should track Rose Cotton — watch their positions leaving the stalls, as whichever secures the closer pitch to the leader will have a meaningful positional edge in the home straight.

Soft ground at Yarmouth over 1m2f will stretch the field considerably — watch for any runner who struggles to hold its position in the first half-mile, as the race shape is likely to be more decisively set by the 4f mark than the pace map suggests.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Facilities Management Front Runner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a handy record over 7f on good, but his only soft-going run produced a solid third (3/15 sim-going) and this drop to 6f with apprentice Mason Paetel (3lb claim) is interesting — 33 days off is fresh enough, and George Margarson's yard is quiet (0/5 in 14 days), so the angle is form rather than stable confidence.
runners_data.comment: Noble Guest shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here in reasonable nick after 33 days away, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 73 suggests he merits respect off a mark of 64.

runners_data.name: Sam's Xpress
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field, Julia & Shelley Birkett's six-year-old has been racing primarily over 5f recently and this step up to 6f on soft ground is the key question — if the extra furlong on testing ground catches them late, the prominent chasers will pounce, but a solo lead with no pressure is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Von Krolock
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has won twice at Standard over 6f (1/6f/STA twice in recent history) and Christian Howarth's 3lb claim keeps the weight competitive; the trainer has been firing (2/41 in 14 days) and this is his most suitable trip and style scenario in the race.
runners_data.comment: Von Krolock arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, but our rating of 58 ranks him tenth of eleven, and he faces a stiff task off 137 lb against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Methgal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 6f on Good recently and also placed over 7f; the tongue-tie and breast-girth combo (hg:tb) suggests a horse that has required management, and Kyle McHugh's 7lb claim is useful, though soft-going form is limited (4/15 sim-going, no wins) and Dylan Cunha's yard has been busy and productive (6/26 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Methgal arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a runner-up finish two starts back gives him a consistent recent profile, though a seventh three starts back highlights the inconsistency that keeps him a midfield proposition under 136 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Insuspense
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a striking run of placed efforts (three 2nds from the last five), though the single soft-going run was a fifth and the 86-day absence is a concern for sharpness; Paddy Bradley takes the ride and the headgear (tongue-tie) is retained, but this race shape — moderate tempo, few genuine closers ahead of them — makes their task harder.
runners_data.comment: Insuspense has been a model of consistency with four seconds in her recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going, making her a genuine threat carrying 136 lb from stall six; the concern is she's been winless in her last six outings and returns after an 86-day absence.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway's five-year-old has a soft-ground win (1/6f/SOF) in the locker and has placed three times from five recent turf starts, giving the best soft-ground profile of the hold-up types; Jack Mitchell is a strong booking, but a blinkered hold-up horse needs more pace than Sam's Xpress alone is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Court Drive shaped well when third three starts back and arrives here fit enough after 24 days off, with experience of today's distance and going in her favour and a solid rating to underpin her claims; the main risk is her most recent sixth leaving something to prove at the top of her form.

runners_data.name: Danger Alert
runners_data.note: An authentic hold-up horse pushed into the mapped midfield here because the field is overloaded with closers — Pat Cosgrave is a telling jockey booking and the horse has good placed runs over this trip, but 99 days off is a significant flag and on this shape, racing beyond their natural deep position, the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 is a genuine discount.
runners_data.comment: Danger Alert is the top-rated runner on our figures and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat from stall one, though he is yet to win in his last five starts and a 99-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Deadline
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's three-year-old is a hold-up type with a short form string (just four runs) and all recent efforts have been in the lower half of the field; Edward Greatrex takes the ride and the youth of the horse means soft going is uncertain, though the lower weight (134lbs) relative to the older horses is a marginal plus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Deadline faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround of 17 days, and carries 134 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Woolridge
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's four-year-old carries a hood (hg:p) and is a genuine closer whose last five runs are all mid-to-back finishes on Standard or Good — pushed into the map's midfield by sheer volume of hold-up types, the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 correctly flags a horse unlikely to find its natural rhythm in this shape; 12 days between runs keeps the horse fresh.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Woolridge does offer some encouragement with a third three starts back, though fifth last time out and a cold trainer spell of 0/24 temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 133 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: My Mate Kev
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is an upgrade in jockey quality for Chris Dwyer's four-year-old, but the horse has been consistently mid-to-back in recent runs and its best effort (2/6f/STA) came from a prominent position on Standard — here it will be mapped further forward than it naturally races, and soft-going form is absent (sim-going: 0W0P from two tries), making the style compromise doubly costly.
runners_data.comment: My Mate Kev shaped with promise when runner-up last time out, though he has been winless in his last five starts overall and that patchy recent record — including finishes of sixth and seventh in the two runs prior — gives pause; he has run over today's trip and going, returns on a fresh 12-day break, and carries 132 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Kyoto
runners_data.note: Mike Murphy's four-year-old has a neat placed record over 6f (three consecutive placed efforts on Standard, one second on soft) but is genuinely a hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield map position; 81 days off is the longest absence in the field and the single soft-going run (5/6f/SOF) offers minimal encouragement — Daniel Muscutt is a competent pick-up but the circumstances stack against.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and rated just 58 on our figures — ranked 9 of 11 — Kyoto has at least run over today's trip and is rated 56 officially, but 81 days off the track and a form profile going the wrong way make him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Sam's Xpress is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful rival to press them from the gates, Dylan Hogan can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits on soft Yarmouth ground over 6f. Von Krolock and Noble Guest are the most likely to track from prominent positions, with Methgal also capable of racing close to the pace, creating a structured front group but not a contested, heated gallop. The soft going will stretch the field and reward those who can travel economically into the race rather than those forced wide or into a sprint finish from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can slot in behind Sam's Xpress early and pounce before the final furlong — hold-up horses face a stiffer task than usual because the tempo, though honest in soft conditions, is unlikely to be frantic enough to create a true end-to-end test. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Danger Alert, Woolridge, My Mate Kev, and Kyoto are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they are unlikely to secure a position that truly suits them, with Sam's Xpress setting a pace that may simply not be strong enough to bring them into the race late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sam's Xpress Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Xpress leads uncontested and sets a soft-ground-appropriate tempo that the hold-up horses cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: Sam's Xpress dictates from the front at a pace that suits soft going, never getting into trouble and conserving enough energy to hold on up the straight; Von Krolock or Noble Guest, tracking in second and third, are best placed to capitalise if Sam's Xpress tires but the leader may simply never be headed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Von Krolock or Noble Guest travel powerfully into the race and collar Sam's Xpress in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With the pace set by Sam's Xpress not fast enough on soft ground to fully test prominent chasers, Von Krolock (whose 6f-Standard/Stable form is solid) and Noble Guest can move smoothly past the leader approaching the final furlong; this shape rewards horses with a clean passage from a handy pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Xpress over-reaches on soft going and ties up late, opening the door for midfield runners finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: Court Drive, who won over 6f on soft going, and Insuspense, with a strong placed record at this trip, have the soft-ground profile to finish fastest of all if the front-runners empty late; however, the redistributed hold-up horses — Danger Alert, My Mate Kev, Woolridge, Kyoto — are racing out of their natural position and their ability to deliver their typical late thrust is compromised by the compressed shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If crowding out of the gates or a false-starting dash scrambles the early order entirely.
scenarios.body: In a muddled scenario where Sam's Xpress is hampered or loses the rail, the race becomes genuinely open and the redistribution of hold-up types into midfield suddenly becomes less of a disadvantage; Deadline and Woolridge could figure if the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Sam's Xpress's stamina for 6f on soft ground is unproven — watch early fractional splits; if they begin to labour approaching the final two furlongs, Von Krolock and Noble Guest are poised to strike.

Yarmouth 6f is a flat, straight track where position off the pace matters enormously on soft going — Danger Alert, Woolridge, My Mate Kev and Kyoto are all genuine closers racing out of their natural role; if any of these get detached early, their chance is effectively gone.

The trainer angle on Methgal (Dylan Cunha 6/26 in 14 days) is notable — a yard in form with a horse that has just won over this course and distance could be underestimated if connections believe soft going is manageable.

Court Drive won over 6f on soft ground and Jack Mitchell's booking lifts confidence — monitor market moves; if this horse is supported, it signals that connections feel the pace will be strong enough to bring a hold-up style into play.

Von Krolock (Christian Howarth, 3lb claim) has two wins at 6f on Standard and the trainer has placed two from 41 runners in 14 days — the apprentice claim makes the weight attractive and the horse's natural style suits tracking Sam's Xpress directly.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Commercial Fit-out Challenge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent form placing at Goodwood, but all five last runs have been on good ground — the soft surface here is an unknown; Ian Williams in fair 14-day form and Harry Davies a competent booking, but a true hold-up from the rear is a tough assignment in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and arrives here in peak freshness just seven days on, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the main risk is that his two efforts before that victory were well below par.

runners_data.name: Cuban Girl
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has placed twice on similar going (2 from 13 sim-going runs), but stepping back up to 7f after a run of 10f efforts and the trip may be sharp; Brian Toomey's yard has only one runner in the past 14 days from a very small book of entries.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Girl shaped with promise when a second three starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going, she appeals as a genuine each-way threat from stall 13 — though winless in her last five starts remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: Gemini Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with soft-ground experience including a run on soft at Haydock and another on soft at Southwell — 6 from 15 on similar surfaces suggests she handles it; the 10-day turnaround and Dylan Hogan booking are neutral, but she remains without a win from 15 comparable-going starts.
runners_data.comment: Gemini Star shaped well when second two starts back and returns refreshed on ten days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; winless in her last five starts, but our ratings mark her as the one to beat here under 134 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a sharp recent form string of 1-3-1-3 and winning form at Yarmouth's sister Flat tracks — David Simcock pair in this race, hold-up style will mean a straight-line challenge in the soft, but the class reading (OR 59) and Daniel Muscutt aboard are among the stronger angles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back and has experience of today's trip and ground, but third last time out hints at inconsistency, and 38 days off adds a fitness query for Campani, who carries 134 lb from stall 14 in a competitive 14-runner heat.

runners_data.name: Pickering Castle
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse placed into midfield by the mapping tool because the rear is oversubscribed — all five recent runs have been at Sandown and the form reads 6-7-7-8-8; no soft-ground evidence in the last five runs and little form to encourage at any going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and without a top-six finish since his most recent run, Pickering Castle faces a stiff task from stall five carrying 131 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 64 suggests he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Potters Prince
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up racer operating without his preferred position in this shape; returning after 141 days off is a significant concern, and while the recent form shows consistent mid-pack finishes on good-to-firm/standard, there is no soft-ground evidence in the record.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Potters Prince has been largely out of the picture in recent outings, and a 141-day absence does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Court Of Session
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who is essentially a 6f horse — all five recent runs are at 6f and this 7f trip looks a stretch; has worn headgear (visor) and soft-ground experience shows 2 from 15, but no placings on similar going and the Phil McEntee yard has 0 wins from 6 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Showed ability when winning four starts back, but three subsequent efforts have been modest at best; has run over today's trip and going, and 12 days between runs suggests he returns fresh, though 131 lb from stall 12 is no easy task.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has won twice on good ground at 8f but is making a rare foray onto soft (only 1 run from 13 in sim-going conditions); natural hold-up racer displaced from the rear by the crowded field — the OR 55 and Kieran O'Neill booking are modest, but the winning form over further suggests staying stamina.
runners_data.comment: Desert Charm drops to a lowly ranking of 12th in a field of 14 on our figures, and her latest effort — eighth last time out — does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back wins three and four starts back show she can find the frame on a good day.

runners_data.name: Oh So Perfect
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race with back-to-back 7f wins at Southwell and a consistent record of placing prominently — Mason Paetel's three-pound claim is a useful weight assist; has placed at 7f on all-weather standard going and Appleby's yard is 1 from 15 in 14 days, but the race shape is built around this horse.
runners_data.comment: Oh So Perfect won two of her last six starts and was second two starts back, bringing strong recent form into this, and she has experience of today's trip and going; the worry is that a fourth last time out leaves her needing to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa's mount is a hold-up horse that the map has moved forward because the rear is saturated — the best recent run is a second at 6f on good, and stepping to 7f on soft for Loughnane (0 from 12 in 14 days) with a STYLE_FIT flag means she is unlikely to race where the scenario needs her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yoko does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and steps back in from stall two, though her latest ninth leaves her with plenty to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Captive Beauty
runners_data.note: Has a ⚠ fade flag in her profile and the going-close record shows 2 from 5 on soft — she has finished 8th twice on soft recently and has not placed in any of those soft runs; a hold-up type held back from her natural slot, and the finishing tendency to weaken does not help in a shape where late running is the only avenue.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of fourteen, Captive Beauty showed a flash of promise with a second two starts back but has otherwise disappointed, and while she has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 17-day break, she faces a stiff task off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Withoutfurtherado
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer mapped to midfield because of field congestion at the rear — the 10-day turnaround is short for a horse without a win from its last nine, and soft-ground record (4 from 15) has produced only one placing; Liam Wright's three-pound claim is some compensation on weight but not in race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Withoutfurtherado at least returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions, though a ninth last time out and a modest official rating of 52 leave him fighting for minor honours from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a recent win at 7f on good and placed at 8f — soft going is a question (1 from 10 in similar conditions, 0 wins), but she steps back to a trip she has won over; Grace McEntee for McEntee's yard (0 from 3 in 14 days), hold-up type who must make ground from a congested midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of these on our figures and carrying a stiff 121 lb from stall 10, Caitlin G is hard to fancy despite her win two starts back; a fifth last time out and modest recent form otherwise leave her needing significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (tongue-tie and visor) and is racing just four days after a previous outing — the soft-ground record is limited (1 from 15) and all five last runs show she finishes in the rear third of the field; a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map with a STYLE_FIT discount and no compelling evidence to suggest she can reverse that pattern here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Rokuni is hard to fancy at the weights, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table and, drawn in stall one, returns just four days after a third two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Perfect is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine early pace pressure — the remainder of the field is entirely hold-up in profile, meaning she can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the gates. On soft ground at Yarmouth over 7f, a lone leader setting a sustainable gallop is a significant tactical advantage; the field will be forced to chase her down rather than sit on her back, and she has already won twice over this exact trip and surface type at Southwell. The redistribution flag is notable: Yoko, Captive Beauty, Potters Prince, Withoutfurtherado, Caitlin G and others are all natural hold-up types mapped forward only because there is nowhere else to put them — in reality, this race will stretch back significantly from Oh So Perfect, with a dense cluster of closers hunting her down in the straight. This shape strongly favours Oh So Perfect's front-running profile and any hold-up performer with a high cruising speed capable of picking up ground quickly on a track that does not genuinely test staying stamina at 7f.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Perfect is allowed to roll into an uncontested lead and sets a soft-to-fair tempo on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: She controls every yard, rations her effort, and the deep field of hold-up types is left with a concerted but ultimately futile closing challenge on a track that rewards front-side bias.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Burst Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the tempo enough that one of the quicker closers can unleash a sustained finish from midfield.
scenarios.body: The pace dulls slightly under conditions, allowing a well-handicapped closer with genuine soft-ground form to reel in the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pressing Horse Wears Down
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent-placed runner escapes the rear cluster and tracks Oh So Perfect closely, forcing her into a stronger gallop.
scenarios.body: The front-runner is softened by early pressure and weakens in the final 100 yards, handing the race to the horse that pressed and stayed on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the backmarkers produce a mass late rally.
scenarios.body: A strong-finishing hold-up type with a soft-ground affinity powers through a tired field, but this requires a materially faster tempo than Oh So Perfect is likely to set given the absence of rivals.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Perfect's sectionals leaving the gates — if she establishes a clear two-length lead inside the first furlong unchallenged, the probability of Scenario A rises sharply and no rival is well-placed to respond given the all-hold-up profile behind her.

Campani and Desert Charm are the two hold-up runners with the sharpest recent form (1-3-1-3 and 1-1-2-8) — watch whether Daniel Muscutt or Kieran O'Neill commits early enough to make ground down the outside before the straight narrows, as hesitation will leave them too far back in the soft.

The 141-day absence of Potters Prince is a significant fitness flag — if he performs well first time out after that layoff it would be a training performance worth noting for future reference, but in the race itself he must be treated as at a disadvantage.

Court Of Session is a 6f specialist on the evidence who is being asked to stay 7f on soft ground — if he fades sharply turning for home it confirms the distance is beyond him and the trail of horses behind him may find their run blocked momentarily.

Yoko with Silvestre De Sousa is the most interesting of the redistributed runners — if De Sousa elects to push forward from the gate rather than settle back, he could slot into a prominent position that the race map shows as unoccupied behind Oh So Perfect, which would make Yoko a genuine Scenario C player.

races.name: Gold & Silver Exchange Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Symphony Of Joy
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile suits the expected late-run scenario; Soft ground is no concern on his OK tag, but inconsistent form figures including a run of 6-11-7 suggest he needs things to fall perfectly, and 27 days since last run is acceptable for Kevin & Lauren Frost's yard.
runners_data.comment: Symphony Of Joy steps up as a leading danger here, having run over today's trip and going, and his third two starts back shows he can threaten at this level; the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's yard is in strong form (T14: 3/28) and Jack Callan takes the ride; his one soft-ground run produced a win over 8f at Sandown, giving him the key sim-going credential in this field, and his recent second over 8f at Goodwood shows he handles this trip.
runners_data.comment: Piazza has struck form at the right time, winning last time out and runner-up two starts back, and she has experience of both today's trip and going. Carrying 142 lb from stall seven, she is the one to beat on her current trajectory.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f at Goodwood and returns just six days later — trainer John Ryan is firing (T14: 2/6), but his natural instinct is to come from off the pace and he is likely to find himself further forward than ideal given the hold-up congestion, softening his edge in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ecclefechan arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims at a mark of 63, and our rating of 69 places him second among the eight runners; the main concern is just six days between runs, which tests his recovery.

runners_data.name: Captain Corelli
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old returning after 283 days off, carrying 135lbs with headgear — the layoff alone is a significant flag, and while Julie Camacho's yard is quiet (T14: 0/15), he would need to recapture form from a string of placed efforts that now feel some way behind him; a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 283-day absence, Captain Corelli faces a stiff ask here, ranked seventh of eight on our figures; he has run over today's distance and going, and stall five is his draw.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record in his last six runs including three thirds suggests he finds a way to be involved; the hood stays on and his hold-up instincts mean he is likely further back than his style-fit position implies, but Matt Crawley's yard is quiet (T14: 0/2) and there is no soft-ground form to draw confidence from.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Rambler has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing second two starts back and third three starts back, and he returns fit on 30 days' rest having run over today's trip and going — yet to win in his last six outings is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts over longer trips suggest stamina is the weapon, and his sim-going run over 9f (placed) gives some encouragement on cut ground; however, Ashley Lewis rides and the horse is squeezed into midfield away from its natural trailing position — the style-fit tag (0.90) rightly tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Big Alex Walmsley nevertheless showed consistency with back-to-back thirds in his two runs before last, and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before; the 134 lb burden from stall one may test his resolve.

runners_data.name: Meritocratic
runners_data.note: Dropped back from ten furlongs to a mile here and that trip compression on soft ground could suit a stayer with a late kick; James Owen is in decent form (T14: 2/41) and Mason Paetel takes the ride, though 70 days off and a hold-up style crammed into midfield make this a speculative angle rather than a confident one.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 70 days off, Meritocratic does have a third two starts back to his name and experience over today's distance and going, but he heads into this rated just 60 and ranked sixth of eight, making a midfield showing the realistic ceiling here.

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's yard managed one win from four runners recently (T14: 1/4) and Connor Planas rides; this horse's natural style is hold-up but is the most forward type in the field and thus maps to the lead — its soft-going record of one placing from 14 attempts (0W0P) is a stark caution, and sustaining a front-running role is firmly out of character.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a pair of seconds in recent form her only encouragement, Amarachi has struggled for consistency and ranks last on our figures here, making her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and returning on a handy 17-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Amarachi is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front, though as a natural hold-up type redistributed to the lead, the gallop is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than truly punishing on this soft Yarmouth mile. With the remainder of the field — Crimson Rambler, Ecclefechan, Meritocratic, Captain Corelli, and Big Alex Walmsley — all genuine hold-up horses jostling for midfield berths, the race shape should be orderly up front but congested through the pack, with runners forced to cover ground they would not naturally seek. Piazza and Symphony Of Joy, also hold-up types, complete a field that is overwhelmingly rear-biased, meaning the winner is almost certain to come from off the pace when Amarachi's modest lead is eventually reeled in. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horse with the best late kick on soft ground, with a premium on horses that can find clear air through a bunched midfield pack in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amarachi Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Amarachi settles into an uncontested rhythm and the soft ground saps the pace of hold-up challengers, leaving the leader in front longer than expected.
scenarios.body: Amarachi dictates every fraction alone and the soft ground acts as a leveller, preventing the hold-up pack from closing efficiently in the straight. A front-runner's dream scenario on a day when the Yarmouth mile rewards those who conserve energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Powers Through
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground tests stamina and the hold-up horses find clear runs to deliver their challenges simultaneously in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Amarachi's modest gallop sets a tempo that appears sedate but grinds on soft ground, and the horses with the best soft-going form and genuine staying power pick them off in the closing stages. Piazza's recent course win at a similar trip and Symphony Of Joy's hold-up pedigree give them the profile for this dominant shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield runners — Crimson Rambler or Ecclefechan — secures a forward enough berth and uses it to land a telling blow turning in.
scenarios.body: Soft ground can sometimes compress the field into a false sense of slow pace before a burst of acceleration tests the hold-up horses, and a runner that has slipped into a handy position may catch the closers flat-footed. Crimson Rambler's consistent placed form and Ecclefechan's recent win give them the credentials to exploit this shape, though their style-fit tags mean this is a discounted likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates further and the race turns into a slog, with fitness and weight-carrying ability separating the field from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A true stamina test on heavy-ish ground can render tactics irrelevant and elevate the horse with the best recent outing and lightest burden, with Meritocratic's step back in trip from ten furlongs giving it an athletic profile for this shape. Big Alex Walmsley's placed efforts over ten furlongs suggest it stays strongly, though its style-fit concern and long odds reflect the uncertainty of this shape materialising.

watchPoints.text: Piazza is the standout soft-ground qualifier in the field — watch whether Jack Callan settles him smoothly in the rear third, as a clean run from that position would give him the ideal passage for a late challenge.

Amarachi's ability to control the pace is central to the race shape — if Connor Planas cannot find a rhythm on the lead or is pressured by a rival hustling up early, the entire scenario structure shifts and runners may hit the front sooner than expected.

The congested midfield, with Crimson Rambler, Ecclefechan, Meritocratic, Big Alex Walmsley and Captain Corelli all naturally wanting to be held up, creates a significant risk of traffic problems in the straight — watch for any runner that secures clear daylight on the outside turning in.

Captain Corelli's 283-day absence combined with 135lbs and a soft surface is a significant compound risk factor — monitor market move or any late withdrawal that might loosen the field and give more room to genuine hold-up horses.

Ecclefechan returns just six days after its Goodwood win — watch whether Christian Howarth rides it more prominently than usual, which could indicate trainer intent to exploit its forward position in the race map rather than fight back to its natural trailing style.
